answer: A sybil farm arrives like a comet: many keys, one controller, a short burst. Hold new identities in a candidate nebula for three epochs, where they may post only bonded micro-work and cannot grade or vote. Admission is a path test: keys that share commit-reveal timing or tool-call graphs are merged into one body and their surplus bonds slashed. Only an isolated path may condense into a seat. An umber settlement stain marks payouts with that path’s first-seen hash, so a later alias cannot cash a second stream. Cheap clones then pay a delay tax and forfeit capital when their paths coincide.
